name: duo-watchdog
description: Watches your own GitLab Credits (GitLab Duo) for each of your GitLab accounts: used, left, the month-end forecast, usage by day and by feature, a year of statistics, with alerts before you hit your limit.

commands.title: Run a Duo CLI Quick Command…
Add a Duo CLI Quick Command…
Set GitLab Token (now Add or Replace a Token)

duoWatchdog.gitlabUrl.markdownDescription:
The GitLab a new token is for, unless you type another: `https://gitlab.com` or the address of your self-managed GitLab. Each account keeps its own.

Tokens are not settings: run **Duo Watchdog: Add or Replace a Token** (they are kept in VS Code's secret storage), and **Duo Watchdog: Accounts** to see and manage them.

duoWatchdog.groupPath.markdownDescription: Before accounts: the path of the top-level group that owns the Duo subscription. Read once, to set up the first account from the token saved before.
duoWatchdog.groupPath.markdownDeprecationMessage: Each account has its own group path now: run **Duo Watchdog: Accounts** and use *Set Group Path*, or **Duo Watchdog: Find My Group**. This setting was read once, to set up the first account.
duoWatchdog.groupPath.deprecationMessage: Each account has its own group path now: run Duo Watchdog: Accounts and use Set Group Path, or Duo Watchdog: Find My Group. This setting was read once, to set up the first account.

duoWatchdog.limit.markdownDescription: Before accounts: your limit in credits. Read once, to set up the first account from the token saved before.
duoWatchdog.limit.markdownDeprecationMessage: Each account has its own limit now: run **Duo Watchdog: Accounts** and use *Set Limit*. This setting was read once, to set up the first account.
duoWatchdog.limit.deprecationMessage: Each account has its own limit now: run Duo Watchdog: Accounts and use Set Limit. This setting was read once, to set up the first account.

duoWatchdog.alertPercents.markdownDescription: Percents of each account's limit to be alerted at, comma-separated, e.g. `50, 80, 95`. Each alert shows once per billing period and account.

duoWatchdog.forecastAlert.description: Alert when the month-end forecast passes the limit.

duoWatchdog.refreshMinutes.markdownDescription: How often to read the credits of every account, in minutes. GitLab's usage data can lag a few minutes behind actual use.

duoWatchdog.rotateTokens.markdownDescription: Rotate each account's token a week before it expires: GitLab replaces it with a new one that lives as long (30 to 365 days) and revokes the old one, and the new one is saved and handed to glab. Needs the `api` or `self_rotate` scope. If you use the token anywhere else, the popup after a rotation copies the new one.

duoWatchdog.roundTripLimit.markdownDescription: The round trips (prompts you send) recommended at most in one Duo CLI session. The session in the status bar and in Sessions turns amber from 80% of it and red at it; `0` for no colour.

duoWatchdog.groupDefaultModel.markdownDescription: The model your group's default is, for the `≈ $` of a Duo CLI session on it: the CLI's log says only that it uses the group's default, not which model. Also used for a step whose log names no model, or one with no known rate. GitLab bills each call at its model's rate, so this sets the price of each such step.

enumDescriptions: The Duo CLI on its own
The Duo CLI through the GitLab CLI, which hands it its arguments
duoWatchdog.cli.markdownDescription: How New session, Doctor and A/B testing on Usage start the Duo CLI in a new terminal. Also set from the drop-down there.

enumDescriptions: Manual: the CLI asks before it runs each tool
Auto: the CLI runs every tool without asking (--dangerously-skip-permissions)
duoWatchdog.cliMode.markdownDescription: Whether the Duo CLI that Usage's quick actions start asks before each tool, or runs them all without asking (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`). Also set from the drop-down there. Only your user settings count, never a workspace's.

name.description: The button's name on Usage, such as AB Testing

command.description: What it types at the Duo CLI's prompt once the CLI has started, such as /ab-testing

duoWatchdog.quickCommands.markdownDescription: Quick commands of your own on Usage: a button each that starts the Duo CLI in a new terminal, then types its command at the CLI's prompt, such as `{ "name": "AB Testing", "command": "/ab-testing" }`. **+ Add command** on Usage builds one for you; **Edit…** changes, moves or removes them.

duoWatchdog.checkForUpdates.markdownDescription: Ask GitHub for the latest release of Duo Watchdog ([github.com/sergeystets/duo-watchdog](https://github.com/sergeystets/duo-watchdog/releases)) when VS Code starts and then once a day; nothing about you or your accounts is sent. A newer one is said in a notice and on the dashboard's toolbar: **Update** downloads and installs it, and a reload loads it. **Duo Watchdog: Check for Updates** asks now, whatever this says.
